document: FICTIONAL TEST DOCUMENT. Fable Harbor Workspace is an invented project-board subscription costing $30 per month. It renews monthly unless the customer cancels by 23:59 UTC on the calendar day before the next billing date. Cancellation stops the next renewal and access continues until the end of the current paid period. Payments are not refunded merely because the customer cancels mid-month. A duplicate charge is an exception: the duplicate amount is refunded in full if reported within thirty calendar days of that charge. Ordinary provider liability is capped at the subscription fees actually paid during the three months preceding the claim. That cap does not apply to fraud or to unauthorized disclosure of the customer's confidential documents. Separately, lost profits are excluded unless they were directly caused by the provider's fraud. Unauthorized disclosure alone is not an exception to the lost-profits exclusion. An exception to the liability cap does not, by itself, override the separate lost-profits exclusion. These are invented contractual terms only; no real service or legal rule is described.
situation: I run an invented design studio. I want to understand renewal and refunds, and compare an ordinary service mistake, an unauthorized disclosure without fraud, and fraud that directly causes lost profits.
